title: What Minneapolis gave him: reading, math and gratitude to teachers
summary: Thomas and Hinton agree that reading and math underlay their careers, and Thomas thanks teachers like Drury; they mention Will Vodery.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: But Minneapolis was really a good place for me, because that's where I learned how to read. I remember that well. Because this guy gave me that book, and sure enough, that Closet(?) book, if you go through and read everything he pointed out to me... He didn't know too much...didn't seem to know too much about tone. Evidently, I have fairly good tone. But he wanted to show me how to read. Because that my stick(?). Because every band I got with, I could read. I remember at one time I could transpose as good as I could read. And I had to go ahead and start learning how to read to read all over again.
I'll bet you were a hundred years ahead of your time. Really.
Yeah, evidently I was. But just like you said, that math did it.
Sure.
I tell so many people, man...
It saved me, man. That saved me.
I'll tell you, that math...
I was in the Math Club in school.

Well, you see, the last two years in Math, there were only about four or five of us in the class. So man, we flew through that class. That's how we could take all them subsequently... That's how we'd take Trigonometry
Thomas - 50
or College Algebra and all that.
That's right.
Because there was nothing to stop us.
That's right.
And then it kind of knocked me out that I was valedictorian of my class. There's one little thing I didn't tell about that, I should...
[END OF TAPE 1, SIDE B]
This teacher was so beautiful, Mr. Drury. You know, you got to be grateful for them people that passed through your life, that showed you...

That's our progress. That's the only way we can progress. That's the reason I feel so dedicated, and I know you do, to trying to do my end... I just feel sad that perhaps I don't think that young people are trying to take advantage of it like you and I took advantage of it, and I wish they would. And I hope that things like this will help them to take advantage of our experiences that came before them.
Right. Because look what a wonderful experience we had with... I almost said Timothy(?) (?)?
With who?
Thomas - 51
With the arranger.
What arranger? Was it Tisdale? Ralph (?)?
No, the arranger from Ziegfield.
Oh, Will Vodery.
Vodery, yes.
Sure.
And he was so wonderful. He'd just stick...
I used to know him! He was twenty-three years with Ziegfield.
Ziegfield, right.
